draft.title: Internal and international migration
card: Migration is the movement of people from one place to live in another. It is sorted by whether the move crosses a country's border.
moving within one country. The person stays in the same country, even if the move is far, such as Perth to Darwin.
moving from one country to another. The person crosses a national border, such as Ireland to Australia.
Distance does not decide the type. A short move across a border is international, and a very long move inside a country is internal.
draft.remember: Internal stays inside a country's border. International crosses it.

a.q: Which move is an example of internal migration?
opts: A family moves from Hobart to Alice Springs
A family moves from Hobart to Auckland
A family moves from Darwin to Dili
A family moves from Adelaide to Singapore
a.why: Hobart and Alice Springs are both in Australia, so the family does not cross a border. The other moves end in another country, so they are international, even though some are shorter trips.
a.clue: Check whether both places are in the same country.

b.q: Priya moves from Perth to Cairns for a new job. Ben moves from Brisbane to Auckland. Priya's trip is longer than Ben's. Which statement is correct?
opts: Priya is internal and Ben is international
Priya is international and Ben is internal
Both are internal, as both stay in the same region
Both are international, as both moves are long
b.why: Priya stays in Australia, so her move is internal, even though it is very long. Ben crosses a national border to New Zealand, so his move is international. The tempting answer fails because distance does not decide the type.
b.clue: Ignore the distances and look at the borders.

a.best: A family moves from Hobart to Alice Springs

b.best: Priya is internal and Ben is international
